​
Understanding Hydraulic Grips in Tensile Testing: Benefits, Installation, and Key Considerations
​
In the realm of materials testing, particularly tensile testing, the choice of gripping mechanism is pivotal to obtaining accurate and reliable results. Hydraulic grips have emerged as a preferred solution for testing high-strength materials such as steel and carbon fiber. The below information explains the advantages of hydraulic grips, outlines their installation process, and highlights essential considerations for their effective use.​ Scroll to the bottom of the page for our products. 
​
Advantages of Hydraulic Grips
Consistent Clamping Force: Hydraulic grips maintain a constant clamping force on the specimen throughout the test, compensating for material necking and ensuring uniform load application. This consistency enhances the repeatability and accuracy of test results.​
High Load Capacity: Designed to withstand substantial forces, hydraulic grips are ideal for testing robust materials like steel and carbon fiber. Their robust construction allows for the application of significant loads without compromising grip integrity.​
Versatility: Hydraulic grips can accommodate a wide range of specimen sizes and geometries, making them suitable for diverse testing applications.​
Ease of Use: Many hydraulic grip systems feature user-friendly controls that facilitate quick and secure specimen loading and unloading, enhancing laboratory efficiency.​
Installation of Hydraulic Grips
Proper installation of hydraulic grips is crucial for their optimal performance. While specific procedures may vary depending on the manufacturer and model, the general installation process involves:
Preparation: Ensure that the universal testing machine (UTM) is powered off and that all components are clean and free from debris. Verify that all necessary parts, including the hydraulic grips, hydraulic power unit (HPU), hoses, and accessories, are available.​
Mounting the Grips: Attach the hydraulic grips to the UTM's crosshead and base, aligning them according to the manufacturer's specifications. Secure the grips using the provided fixtures, ensuring they are firmly in place.​
Connecting the Hydraulic System: Connect the hydraulic hoses from the HPU to the grips, ensuring that all connections are tight and leak-free. Proper routing of hoses is essential to prevent interference during testing.​
Hydraulic Power Unit Setup: Position the HPU in a suitable location, considering factors such as accessibility and ventilation. Connect the HPU to a power source and fill it with the recommended hydraulic fluid.​
System Bleeding: Remove any air from the hydraulic system by following the manufacturer's bleeding procedure. This step is vital to ensure consistent grip pressure and accurate test results.​
Testing and Calibration: Power on the UTM and HPU, then test the grips' functionality by performing a trial run with a sample specimen. Calibrate the system as necessary to ensure accurate force measurements.​
Key Considerations
Safety: Always adhere to the manufacturer's safety guidelines during installation and operation. Hydraulic systems operate under high pressure, posing potential hazards if mishandled.​
Maintenance: Regularly inspect the hydraulic grips and associated components for signs of wear or damage. Routine maintenance, including checking hydraulic fluid levels and replacing worn parts, is essential for sustained performance.​
Training: Ensure that all personnel involved in operating the hydraulic grips are adequately trained and familiar with the equipment's functions and safety protocols.​
Hydraulic grips are a robust and versatile solution for tensile testing of high-strength materials. Their consistent clamping force, high load capacity, and adaptability make them an invaluable asset in materials testing laboratories. Proper installation and maintenance are key to leveraging their full potential and ensuring accurate, reliable test results.
​
60kN Hydraulic Grip
The 60kN Hydraulic Grips are perfect for lower strength tensile testing and fatigue testing. These grips include a fully integrated hydraulic piston and close from one side. The other side is adjustable by hand. There is also an option for double pistons on the 60kN version.

180kN Hydraulic Grips
The 180kN Hydraulic Grips are designed to test extra wide samples. They are perfect for geotextile tensile testing where samples can be up to 8 inches wide. The grips are available in both single piston and dual piston designs.

100kN Hydraulic Wedge Grips
The 100kN Hydraulic Wedge Grips are "non-shift" wedge grips meaning the grip jaws will stay in their exact place vertically, while the grip body will move up and down to open and close. This type of design is ideal when using extensometer for measuring elongation & strain, as is common with ASTM E8 and ISO 6892.

The 250kN Hydraulic Wedge Grips are similar to the 100kN and are also "non-shift" style wedge grips.
